html:
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the throne of Austria Hungary, and his wife Sophie took place in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914, when Gavrilo Princip, a 19 year old Bosnian Serb, shot them in their car.

Princip belonged to Young Bosnia, a group of students armed with help from the Black Hand, a secret society of Serbian officers. An earlier bomb had missed, and the driver took a wrong turn near the Latin Bridge, where Princip was standing. Austria blamed Serbia and sent it an ultimatum. Russia backed Serbia, Germany backed Austria, and within six weeks the great powers were at war in World War I. The killing grew out of the annexation of Bosnia in 1908.
